failures.criterion: Review finding (mermaid-diagrams.ts:150): one author's diagram must not degrade every reader's Dispatch; drawing cost is bounded
failures.evidence: The worker draws one source at a time, and a cancelled draw (its body re-painted or unmounted) leaves its source queued in `requests` (mermaid-diagrams.ts:312-326: the cancel only clears `target.blocks`), so the worker still draws every source of a page the reader has left, each up to the 5 s limit, before any source of the page they are on. Real surface, chromium, tester lane (throwaway e2e, deleted after the run): issue CORE-1 holds one message with two 450-node flowcharts (27,989 chars); issue CORE-2 holds a message with `graph TD Start --> Finish`. CORE-2 opened alone: its diagram drew in 1.9-2.9 s. CORE-1 opened alone: refusals at 7.0 s and 12.8 s (serial). CORE-1 opened, then an in-app move to CORE-2 (history.pushState + popstate, same document confirmed) 2.7 s later: CORE-2's diagram drew 11.7 s after the move, 14.4 s after CORE-1 loaded, so it waited for CORE-1's second diagram, which no reader was shown. A full page load (the in-body link is a hard navigation) resets the worker, so only in-app moves (sidebar, tabs, Inbox) carry the queue. An issue holding many slow diagrams therefore stalls every diagram for the rest of the reader's SPA session, 5 s per diagram. Red test: `a source no body still waits for is never sent to the worker` in packages/dispatch/web/src/features/refs/MarkdownBody.test.tsx (commit c9a6c465), shown failing by `cd packages/dispatch && bun test web/src/features/refs/MarkdownBody.test.tsx -t Mermaid` -> 12 pass, 1 fail: `expect(sent.some((source) => source.includes("Gone"))).toBe(false)` received true.
